title: Get Started With Clo! Beginner'S Quick Start Guide
description:
Download the file here to follow along: https://connect.clo-set.com/detail/0fb4d800ccd34dcd89d55aff7568a1cb

In this bite-sized mini workshop, we’ll take you step-by-step through everything you need to kickstart your CLO journey: 
✨ Importing a pattern from CONNECT 
✨ Building your style in CLO 
✨ Adding fabrics, prints & colors 
✨ Rendering a fun final image 

Whether you’re brand new to CLO or just want a refresher, this is the perfect way to dive in and create right alongside us.

markdown_content: ## Introduction to CLO and Connect Platform This section introduces CLO, a 3D fashion design software, and its Connect platform used for sharing and selling 3D assets. It covers downloading essential assets like avatars, patterns, fabrics, and graphics from Connect to start a project in CLO. - CLO is a 3D design software for garment creation. - Connect is CLO’s platform for downloading and selling 3D assets. - Assets include DXF pattern files, PNG textures, tags, graphics, and CLO project files (.PRJ). - ZIP folders must be extracted before importing assets into CLO since CLO cannot directly link zipped files. --- ## CLO User Interface Overview and Version Notes This section explains the CLO user interface (UI) in version 2025.1.2.4.0, highlighting key windows and toolbars used for 3D garment design and pattern editing. - CLO version can be viewed in the lower-left corner of the screen. - The “Library” was moved (from left sidebar to upper right linked icon) in 2025. - Main windows: - **3D Window:** Displays avatar and sewn garments. - **2D Window:** Shows flat patterns and pattern arrangement. - **Object Browser:** On the right, acts like a Bill of Materials showing fabrics, trims, buttons, stitches, etc. - Toolbars on both 2D and 3D sides provide selection, transformation, sewing, and editing tools. - Property Editor displays detailed info about selected objects (fabrics, patterns, graphics). --- ## User Settings and Customization This section covers important user settings to optimize workflow, such as mouse configuration, unit systems, auto-save intervals, shortcuts, and UI appearance. - View Controls: Supports 3-button mouse (recommended), Magic Mouse (commands may differ). - Unit System: Inches (default for US users), centimeters, or millimeters available. - Auto Save: Default is 10 minutes; recommended to reduce to 5 minutes for safety without slowing performance. - Toolbar Grouping: Can be toggled on/off depending on screen size and user preference. - Tooltips and video/manual links can be enabled for learning. - Font size and UI scaling can be adjusted for visibility and monitor resolution. - Default 3D and 2D toolbar placement: left and right sides, respectively. --- ## CLO Library and Asset Management This section explains how to manage asset libraries in CLO, including default CLO assets, linked folders, and custom user libraries. - CLO Library has three main tabs: - **CLO Tab:** Default CLO assets (garments, avatars, fabrics, trims, stages). - **CLO Set Tab:** Cloud collaboration and tech pack tools. - **Connect Tab:** Access to Connect store assets. - Users should NOT save personal assets in default CLO folders to avoid data loss during uninstalls. - Users can link external folders (e.g., “CLO Live” or custom tutorial folders) for asset management. - Libraries can be viewed in icon or list mode; info icons provide metadata. - Assets are added to workspace by right-clicking and selecting “Add to Workspace.” --- ## Importing and Arranging Patterns in CLO This section details importing DXF pattern files and initial arrangement of pattern pieces around the avatar. - Importing DXF files: Use default options like “Add,” “Auto-scale,” “Maintain original grainline,” and include notches. - Patterns imported maintain edges without seam allowances visually for clarity. - Patterns can be arranged in 2D workspace using the Transform Pattern tool (shortcut A). - Symmetric duplication (Ctrl/Cmd + D) creates mirrored pattern pieces with linked editing. - Edit Pattern tool (shortcut Z) allows editing individual points and lines. - Multiple patterns can be unfolded symmetrically at once. - 2D and 3D windows are synchronized for pattern selection and arrangement. --- ## Avatar Import and Management This section explains adding avatars (mannequins, humans, kids, etc.) to CLO projects and applying sizes. - Avatars are .AVT files; sizes are .AVS files. - CLO default avatars include mannequins and realistic models like Luna, Mia, Naomi, and Yuna. - Avatars are necessary to simulate garment draping correctly. - Size variants include EU, ASTM, Missy, Curvy, Petite, Plus, Teenage, Maternity, etc. - Avatars and sizes are applied separately to customize fit. --- ## Navigation and View Controls in CLO This section covers essential navigation controls in CLO’s 2D and 3D windows for efficient modeling. - Zoom: Mouse scroll wheel zooms in/out centered on cursor location. - Pan: Click and hold middle mouse button (scroll wheel) to drag view. - Rotate (3D only): Right-click and drag to orbit around the avatar. - Shortcut “2” centers and fronts the avatar in the 3D view. - 3D view also offers preset camera angles (front, back, top, etc.) via right-click menu. --- ## Sewing Tools and Techniques This section explains CLO’s sewing tools: Segment Sewing, Free Sewing, and Edit Sewing, with examples of usage and fixing sewing errors. - **Segment Sewing:** Two clicks to sew between pattern segment points; good for simple seams. - **Free Sewing:** Four clicks to sew between multiple points or complex curves; useful for continuous seams. - **Edit Sewing:** Used to select, delete, or reverse sewing lines. - Sewing notches must be aligned to avoid twisting seams. - Symmetric sewing automatically applies sewing to mirrored pattern pieces. - One-to-Multiple sewing applies one pattern piece’s edge to multiple edges on others (e.g., sleeve cap to front and back armholes). - Sewing errors can be fixed by reversing sewing direction. --- ## Simulating Garment Draping and Adjusting Particle Distance This section covers garment simulation basics and particle distance settings for mesh resolution and simulation quality. - Simulation is toggled via the spacebar or 3D toolbar button. - Simulation modes: Normal (default), Fitting Accurate (slow but precise), Animation. - Particle Distance controls mesh density (default 20 for large pieces): - Larger pieces: keep at 20 for performance. - Medium pieces (e.g., sleeves): 10 for smoother draping. - Small pieces (e.g., neck bands, pockets): 5 for high resolution/detail. - Smaller particle distance improves smoothness but slows down simulation. - Mesh display toggle shows the triangle mesh used for garment simulation. --- ## Applying and Managing Fabrics This section explains how to select, add, and assign fabrics from CLO’s library, including color, texture, and fabric properties. - Fabrics are accessed from CLO library under “Fabrics” tab. - Download fabrics if not already installed (indicated by “N” icon). - Assign fabrics by dragging onto pattern pieces or using the Assign button after selecting multiple pieces. - Fabric properties in Property Editor: - Base color map can be switched or customized. - Fabric type affects visual appearance but not physical simulation. - Color can be selected via CLO’s color picker, Pantone, YKK, or Coloro palettes. - Unused fabrics can be deleted from the Object Browser. --- ## Editing Patterns and Adding Details This section details pattern editing commands such as offsetting outlines, adding points, splitting lines, and creating new pattern pieces like pockets. - Offset Pattern Outline allows extension/retraction of pattern edges (e.g., lengthening skirt hem by 1 inch). - Edit Sewing lines need adjustment after pattern edits to maintain seam alignment. - Polygon and Rectangle tools create new pattern pieces. - Add Point/Split Line tool allows adding points precisely (e.g., to create a 5-point pocket). - Points and lines can be moved with snapping and precision input (e.g., moving a point exactly 0.5 inches down). - Internal lines can be cloned from pattern outlines for sewing reference. --- ## Sewing Pockets Using Internal Lines and Superimpose This section describes sewing a pocket onto a garment using internal lines and the superimpose tool. - Internal lines created by cloning pattern edges serve as sewing targets. - Free Sewing tool is used to sew pocket edges to internal lines. - Superimpose over/under/side snaps smaller pieces onto the main pattern for accurate layering. - Particle distance of small pieces like pockets should be reduced to 5 for better simulation quality. - Internal lines can be adjusted or removed independently of main pattern pieces. --- ## Adding Graphics and Tags This section explains how to add graphics and tags to garments in CLO, including scaling, placement, and face orientation. - Graphics must be added as graphics (right-click > Add as Graphic) rather than dropped directly onto fabric textures. - Graphics can be moved, scaled, and rotated in both 2D and 3D windows using the Transform Graphics tool. - Graphics import at original scale but can be resized precisely using the precision input. - Different print types (solid, blend with fabric, metallic, crack/vintage) affect visual appearance. - Tags can be added similarly as graphics, either by right-click or drag-and-drop into the graphics tab. - Tag face orientation (front/back) can be toggled for inside/outside garment placement. - Avatar display settings can hide/show avatar or tags as needed for visualization. --- ## Creating and Managing Colorways This section covers creating multiple colorways for a garment, applying different fabrics, prints, and colors, and managing them in the Colorway editor. - Colorway editor is accessed via Production > Colorway. - Users can add new colorways by duplicating the current one. - Colorways should be named descriptively. - Fabrics and graphics

sizes are .AVS files. - CLO default avatars include mannequins and realistic models like Luna, Mia, Naomi, and Yuna. - Avatars are necessary to simulate garment draping correctly. - Size variants include EU, ASTM, Missy, Curvy, Petite, Plus, Teenage, Maternity, etc. - Avatars and sizes are applied separately to customize fit. --- ## Navigation and View Controls in CLO This section covers essential navigation controls in CLO’s 2D and 3D windows for efficient modeling. - Zoom: Mouse scroll wheel zooms in/out centered on cursor location. - Pan: Click and hold middle mouse button (scroll wheel) to drag view. - Rotate (3D only): Right-click and drag to orbit around the avatar. - Shortcut “2” centers and fronts the avatar in the 3D view. - 3D view also offers preset camera angles (front, back, top, etc.) via right-click menu. --- ## Sewing Tools and Techniques This section explains CLO’s sewing tools: Segment Sewing, Free Sewing, and Edit Sewing, with examples of usage and fixing sewing errors. - **Segment Sewing:** Two clicks to sew between pattern segment points; good for simple seams. - **Free Sewing:** Four clicks to sew between multiple points or complex curves; useful for continuous seams. - **Edit Sewing:** Used to select, delete, or reverse sewing lines. - Sewing notches must be aligned to avoid twisting seams. - Symmetric sewing automatically applies sewing to mirrored pattern pieces. - One-to-Multiple sewing applies one pattern piece’s edge to multiple edges on others (e.g., sleeve cap to front and back armholes). - Sewing errors can be fixed by reversing sewing direction. --- ## Simulating Garment Draping and Adjusting Particle Distance This section covers garment simulation basics and particle distance settings for mesh resolution and simulation quality. - Simulation is toggled via the spacebar or 3D toolbar button.

Simulation is toggled via the spacebar or 3D toolbar button. - Simulation modes: Normal (default), Fitting Accurate (slow but precise), Animation. - Particle Distance controls mesh density (default 20 for large pieces): - Larger pieces: keep at 20 for performance. - Medium pieces (e.g., sleeves): 10 for smoother draping. - Small pieces (e.g., neck bands, pockets): 5 for high resolution/detail. - Smaller particle distance improves smoothness but slows down simulation. - Mesh display toggle shows the triangle mesh used for garment simulation. --- ## Applying and Managing Fabrics This section explains how to select, add, and assign fabrics from CLO’s library, including color, texture, and fabric properties. - Fabrics are accessed from CLO library under “Fabrics” tab. - Download fabrics if not already installed (indicated by “N” icon). - Assign fabrics by dragging onto pattern pieces or using the Assign button after selecting multiple pieces. - Fabric properties in Property Editor: - Base color map can be switched or customized. - Fabric type affects visual appearance but not physical simulation. - Color can be selected via CLO’s color picker, Pantone, YKK, or Coloro palettes. - Unused fabrics can be deleted from the Object Browser. --- ## Editing Patterns and Adding Details This section details pattern editing commands such as offsetting outlines, adding points, splitting lines, and creating new pattern pieces like pockets. - Offset Pattern Outline allows extension/retraction of pattern edges (e.g., lengthening skirt hem by 1 inch). - Edit Sewing lines need adjustment after pattern edits to maintain seam alignment. - Polygon and Rectangle tools create new pattern pieces. - Add Point/Split Line tool allows adding points precisely (e.g., to create a 5-point pocket). - Points and lines can be moved with snapping and precision input (e.g., moving a point exactly 0.5 inches down). - Internal lines can be cloned from pattern outlines for sewing reference. --- ## Sewing Pockets Using Internal Lines and Superimpose This section describes sewing a pocket onto a garment using internal lines and the superimpose tool. - Internal lines created by cloning pattern edges serve as sewing targets. - Free Sewing tool is used to sew pocket edges to internal lines. - Superimpose over/under/side snaps smaller pieces onto the main pattern for accurate layering. - Particle distance of small pieces like pockets should be reduced to 5 for better simulation quality. - Internal lines can be adjusted or removed independently of main pattern pieces. --- ## Adding Graphics and Tags This section explains how to add graphics and tags to garments in CLO, including scaling, placement, and face orientation.
